title: Custom Robo Arena
subtitle: A school day can end in a robot duel

body: Custom Robo Arena is Noise's Nintendo DS action role-playing game about a young Robo Commander building a reputation in the town of Midheart. Meeting other battlers, entering competitions and confronting the misuse of Robo technology connect the small mechanical contests with a larger adventure. The robot's equipment can be changed before entering a real-time arena fight. Moving between town life and those duels gives the collection of parts a practical destination: another opponent will test the machine the player has assembled and the skill with which it is controlled.

A Robo is built from a body, gun, bomb, pod and legs. Changing those components alters its movement, its available attacks and the range at which it is comfortable fighting. A fast machine with short-range weapons presents a different problem from one prepared to maintain distance. The arena then asks the player to use that arrangement while avoiding the opponent's attacks. Customisation therefore involves deciding how the parts work together, rather than treating every newly acquired component as an automatic improvement over whatever was fitted before it.

Between encounters, the garage allows parts to be changed and arrangements to be prepared for another opponent. The wider adventure supplies new rivals and reasons to revisit that equipment, while multiplayer allows another human player to test it in a direct contest. The touchscreen also provides access to the Soulboost ability during a fight. Custom Robo Arena makes the small robot both a fighting character and a personal construction: its performance depends on the decisions made before the duel as well as the movement and timing used after the arena opens.
